title: Corneal cross-linking
what: The cornea is soaked with vitamin drops and treated with ultraviolet light. It becomes stronger and changes shape less.
why: Most often for keratoconus, when the cornea gets thinner and the condition is getting worse.
duration: the procedure usually takes about an hour; the surface heals in a few days
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
If you had eye herpes or other eye diseases
If you have an autoimmune disease

prepare.title: Contact lenses
prepare.text: Lenses are usually stopped beforehand. The clinic will tell you how long.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Before the procedure, the thickness and shape of the cornea are measured.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Have someone take you home. You cannot drive.

prepare.title: At home
prepare.text: Get the drops you will be prescribed, and sunglasses.

steps: Numbing drops are put in your eye
A small device holds your eyelid open
The doctor usually removes the thin top layer of the cornea
Vitamin drops are put in several times
Your eye is treated with ultraviolet light while you look at a point
At the end, a soft protective lens is put in
feel: During the procedure, it usually does not hurt
Afterward, for 1 to 3 days, there is pain, stinging, watering, and sensitivity to light
Vision may be worse than usual for the first few weeks
after: Use the drops exactly as the doctor said
Do not rub your eye or remove the protective lens yourself
The doctor usually removes the protective lens after a few days
Vision settles over a few months
red_flags: Severe pain that the prescribed medicines do not help
Pus or a white spot on the cornea
The protective lens fell out: contact the clinic

faq.a: The main goal is to stop it from getting worse. Sometimes vision improves a little.

faq.q: Can both eyes be done at once?
faq.a: Usually one at a time. The doctor decides.

reminders.text: Cross-linking tomorrow. Bring sunglasses and arrange for someone to take you home.
